sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Occupant protection, load and trip planning

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A27
The printed infant-seat guide lists children up to 20 pounds, a rear-facing position and a 30-degree recline. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A27
The printed convertible-seat guide lists infants and children up to 40 pounds, with infants reclined rearward and toddlers upright forward-facing. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A27
The printed booster guide lists toddlers weighing at least 30 pounds, requiring a tethered harness or shoulder straps without a shield and allowing a lap belt alone with a shield. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A28
The handbook identifies a child seat as misused if it is not attached with a vehicle belt, its harness is unused or very loose, an infant faces forward, or an available top tether is unused. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A28
The handbook says a seatbelt can be unfastened in under 1 second when addressing the fear of being trapped. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A28
A seatbelt may keep a person conscious in a crash, improving the opportunity to escape even in the uncommon fire or deep-water scenario. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A28
The handbook reports that over half of traffic deaths occur within 25 miles of home and that many occur on roads posted below 45 miles per hour. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A28
Remaining inside the vehicle improves survival chances compared with ejection, and belts help prevent occupants being thrown into another vehicle’s path. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A28
In a side collision, unrestrained occupants move toward the impact point as the vehicle is pushed sideways rather than safely away from it. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A28
The handbook rejects bracing at low speed and uses a 25-mile-per-hour head-on crash analogy involving a fast bicycle striking a brick wall or a fall from a three-story building. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A28
Driving with an unsecured load is illegal and dangerous, and causing a crash through poor load security can lead to fines and jail. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A28
A load is secure only when its contents cannot slide, shift, fall or sift onto the road or become airborne. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A28
Secure a load with rope, netting or straps, fastening large objects directly to the vehicle or trailer. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A28
Consider covering the whole load with a sturdy tarp or net. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A28
Do not overload the vehicle or trailer, and recheck that the load is secure. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A28
Animals carried in a vehicle also need to be secured properly. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A28
Before a trip, decide whether travel is necessary and whether a ride with someone else or available public transportation can meet the need. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A28
Using a car less, including through trip planning, can reduce fuel costs and prolong its life. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A28
Avoid heavy traffic when possible because it adds wear on both the driver and vehicle. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A28
Use carpools or shared rides when possible. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A28
Combine errands by listing needed items and destinations, visiting several places in a trip and reducing unnecessary destinations. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A28
Call ahead to confirm that the needed item is available or the pickup is ready before making the trip. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0028]
